title: Trump's Approval Falls to a Record Low Before the Midterms
summaryZh: 民調顯示川普支持度跌至33%創新低，民主黨期中選舉前領先8個百分點。
summaryHi: मध्यावधि चुनाव से पहले ट्रंप की लोकप्रियता 33% के रिकॉर्ड निचले स्तर पर।
summaryEs: La aprobación de Trump cae al 33 %, mínimo récord antes de las legislativas.
summaryJa: 中間選挙を前にトランプ氏の支持率が33%と過去最低に。
summaryKo: 중간선거를 앞두고 트럼프 지지율이 33%로 최저치를 기록했다.
summaryEn: A new poll puts Trump's approval at 33%, his lowest ever, before the midterms.
paragraphs: President Donald Trump's approval rating has dropped to 33 percent, the lowest point of either term, according to a Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll discussed on PBS NewsHour.
The survey also gives Democrats an eight-point advantage ahead of November's midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress.

Support within Trump's own party is divided. Among Republicans who identify with his MAGA movement, his approval stands at 94 percent, but among other Republicans he is barely breaking even, with almost half disapproving.

NPR's Tamara Keith noted that at a September dinner, Trump promised Republicans in tight races he would visit 35 competitive districts. Her analysis suggests he has managed fewer than a third, mostly in safely Republican areas.

Carrie Dann of the Cook Political Report highlighted Ohio, where the Senate contest has attracted more advertising money than any other since September 1. Both analysts also pointed to Trump's controversial plan to overhaul a historic public golf course in Washington, which has triggered a legal battle.
A new poll asked Americans what they think of President Trump. Only 33 percent said he is doing a good job. This is his lowest number in both of his times as president.
There is an important election in November. It is called the midterm election. In the poll, the Democrats are 8 points ahead of the Republicans.
Most of Trump's strong fans still like him. But many other Republicans do not.
Trump said he would visit 35 places with close races. A reporter says he has visited fewer than a third of them.
In Ohio, people are spending a lot of money on TV ads for the Senate race. It is the most expensive Senate race since September 1.
President Donald Trump's approval rating has fallen to 33 percent, the lowest of either of his two terms, according to a new Washington Post, ABC News and Ipsos poll.
The poll also shows Democrats leading by eight points before the midterm elections in November, when Americans will vote for members of Congress. This result is bad news for his party.
Trump is still very popular with Republicans who support his MAGA movement: 94 percent of them approve of him. But among other Republicans, almost half disapprove.

NPR reporter Tamara Keith told PBS NewsHour that Trump had promised to visit 35 competitive districts. However, he has visited fewer than a third, mostly in places where Republicans are already strong.

Money is pouring into some races. In Ohio, the Senate race has had the most advertising spending of any Senate race since September 1. Meanwhile, Trump's plan to rebuild a historic public golf course in Washington has led to a legal fight.

Carrie Dann of the Cook Political Report highlighted Ohio, where the Senate contest has attracted more advertising money than any other since September 1. President Donald Trump's approval rating has slumped to 33 percent, a low for either of his terms, according to a Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll analysed on PBS NewsHour.
The findings hand Democrats an eight-point edge heading into November's midterms, which will determine which party controls Congress for the remainder of his presidency.

The figures expose a fault line within the Republican Party. While 94 percent of MAGA-aligned Republicans still back the president, the rest of the party is far more ambivalent, with almost half voicing disapproval.

NPR's Tamara Keith observed that Trump had pledged to campaign in 35 competitive districts, yet has visited fewer than a third, largely sticking to reliably Republican territory rather than battleground seats.

Carrie Dann of the Cook Political Report singled out Ohio, whose Senate race has drawn more advertising spending than any other since September 1. The analysts also flagged the president's contentious bid to redevelop a historic public golf course in Washington, now mired in litigation.
President Donald Trump's approval rating has plummeted to 33 percent, the lowest figure recorded in either of his terms, according to a Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll examined on PBS NewsHour.
Significantly, the survey gives Democrats an eight-point lead ahead of November's midterm elections, the outcome of which will determine control of Congress.

The data reveal a pronounced divide within the Republican electorate. Whereas 94 percent of MAGA-affiliated Republicans continue to endorse the president, the remainder of the party is considerably more sceptical, with nearly half expressing disapproval.

NPR's Tamara Keith remarked that, although Trump had pledged to campaign in 35 competitive districts, he has visited fewer than a third of them, predominantly confining himself to dependable Republican strongholds.

Furthermore, Carrie Dann of the Cook Political Report emphasised that Ohio's Senate race has attracted more advertising expenditure than any other since September 1. Both commentators also referred to the president's contentious proposal to redevelop a historic public golf course in Washington, which has provoked a legal dispute.
